Machines in this summary: cloud-vm-4core. Rows tagged `cloud-smoke` (if any) are smoke tests.

Protocol experiments: 100800 rows = profiles x PQ schemes x modes x M x loss conditions x 20 seeds; all means below are over seeds, '±' is the standard deviation over seeds (SE = sd/sqrt(20)).

## Questions, restated for the real experiments

- **Q1 (fit).** Which (scheme, mode) pairs fit one message of each profile's authentication budget? Signatures are scored only against signature spaces, public keys only against key spaces; certificates have an explicit issuer.
- **Q2 (loss, real protocols).** With sender and receiver implemented with real cryptography and byte framing, and every mode given the same slots and bytes per application message: at 0-30% i.i.d. and burst loss, does the PQ-anchored TESLA-style chain (anchor erasure-coded, symmetric to the erasure-coded signature) (H2a) authenticate a larger share of messages, (H2b) use fewer bytes on air per authenticated message, (H2c) authenticate with lower per-message delay, and (H2d) let a late joiner authenticate sooner, than per-message fragmented signatures with MDS coding?
- **Q3 (size vs time).** Is the signature size or the timing tail the binding constraint, and can each sender keep up with the message rate (SLH-DSA)?

## Q1: which (scheme, mode) pairs fit each profile

Sources: `raw/scoring_all_levels.csv` (all classes; appendix), `results/main_table_lowest_level.csv` (lowest level per family), `experiments/profiles.yaml`. **Headers marked [ceiling-based] have no authentication-only budget in their source: budget = payload ceiling minus the stated overheads (one rule for both C-V2X ceilings), so the verdict is conditional on that derivation.**

Byte-accounting formulas (`lib/pqsig/accounting.py`):

```
Byte and frame accounting for authentication modes (single-object fit; loss and latency are measured in lib/pqsig/proto).

Notation: S = declared signature bytes (liboqs OQS_SIG length_signature), P = public-key bytes,
B = profile auth_budget (bytes per message), h = fragment header per message (TODO-RESULT -> 0, flagged),
F1/Fn = payload of the first / later frames of a message, Tm = message period, Tf = frame period.
 frames(x)   = 1 if x <= F1 else 1 + ceil((x - F1)/Fn)         frames needed for x bytes in ONE message
 msgs(x)     = ceil(x / (B - h))                               messages needed when x bytes are spread over messages
 ttfa(x)     = (msgs-1)*Tm + (frames_in_last_message - 1)*Tf   from first fragment to last, no loss, no join wait, no processing
margin = B - x (negative = does not fit, bytes over budget).
Modes (auth object x; `fits` means x <= B, i.e. msgs = 1):
  full            x = S
  full_cert_pq    certificate with an explicit PQ issuer (issuer scheme = subject scheme): cert = P + metadata + S_issuer.
                  steady x = S + digest bytes; peak x = S + P + metadata + S (message signature + certificate); metadata is
                  TODO-RESULT (0 used = lower bound; fit also reported at the two derived sensitivity values). Only for
                  profiles whose source sends a certificate (peak_extra pk+fixed).
  full_cert_cl    the source's classical-issuer case (abrar2026deployment): cert = P + 105 B (metadata + classical issuer
                  signature, derived from the Falcon-512 certificate). Separately labelled; only where the source states it.
  full_cert_pk    bare public key delivered with the signature (peak_extra pk: Remote ID endorsement, DNSKEY): x = S + P
  chain           steady x = tag + key (per message); anchor = S + commit + ts, spread over msgs(anchor) messages;
                  join time = ttfa(anchor) + d*Tm.  `fits` is NOT a meaningful column (the 32 B steady cost always fits): the
                  chain is judged by join time against a deadline (summary.md), not by a fit count.
  hybrid          x = S_partner + S   (partner = the classical scheme the profile's source uses)
  key_delivery    (role public-key-space profiles only) x = P against the key space (OSNMA DSM-PKR); no signature is scored there.
A mode with x > B is not a single-message fit; its cost is the message count and ttfa columns.
share_of_budget = x / B.
```

**OSNMA (fixed).** Signatures are scored only against the DSM-KROOT signature space (`osnma_kroot158`, 158 B derived). Public keys are scored only against the DSM-PKR key space (`osnma_pkr_keys`, 76 B derived = (1632-1024) bit / 8). The former 'PKR as signature budget' column is removed.

## Q2: real protocols on a seeded slot channel

Sources: `raw/proto_results_cloud-vm-4core.csv` (one row per profile x PQ scheme x mode x M x loss condition x seed; aggregated in `results/proto_summary.csv`), `raw/proto_alloc_cloud-vm-4core.csv` (allocation), `lib/pqsig/proto/modes.py` (senders/receivers), `lib/pqsig/proto/oqs.py` (liboqs 0.16.0 through ctypes, `pqshim.c`). A message counts as authenticated only if the receiver verified the received bytes (PQ signature / Merkle root signature / anchor signature plus HMAC chain check, plus Ed25519 for hybrids); `false_accepts` (accepted bytes different from the sent bytes) in all rows: 0.

**Implemented modes** (names in the CSV): `frag_rep` (i: signature fragmented, plain repetition), `frag_mds` (ii: same, Reed-Solomon coded), `merkle4/8/16` (iii: batch signature, per-message authentication path, signature MDS-coded in the next batch's windows), `chain` (iv: TESLA-style chain, 16 B HMAC tags, key disclosed one window later, anchor = commitment + timestamp + PQ signature, MDS-coded across the epoch's slots, anchor wait included in delays), `chain_lead` (anchor of epoch e sent during epoch e-1: removes the steady-state anchor wait, costs join time), `chain_lead_cont` (as chain_lead plus **chain continuity**: the next epoch's commitment is carried inside the MAC input of the current epoch, so a receiver that authenticated epoch e needs no anchor for e+1), `hyb_rep`/`hyb_mds` (v: Ed25519 + PQ signature, both verified).

**Chain continuity across epochs: implemented** (`chain_lead_cont`; negative test T5/T6 below). `chain` and `chain_lead` deliberately do not use it so that the anchor is treated like the erasure-coded signature of (ii).

**Allocation rule (one rule, no hand tuning)** (docstring of `modes.py`):

```
ALLOCATION RULE (identical for all modes, no hand tuning):
  R1 every slot's auth field = header + mode control field + one symbol of the mode's heavy blob, truncated to nothing else;
  R2 symbol room = cap_regular - header - control;  k = ceil(blob / room) source symbols of s = ceil(blob / k) bytes;
     frame length F = header + control + s;
  R3 slot position j is USABLE iff cap(j) >= F (on C-V2X the slot carrying the full certificate usually is not);
  R4 coded modes send n_sym = min(usable slots in the blob's span, 255) MDS symbols round robin over the usable slots
     of the span; repetition modes send the k raw symbols round robin; span = 1 window (frag), n windows (Merkle),
     E windows (chain anchor);
  R5 a mode is infeasible when its span has fewer usable slots than k.
```

Allocation table for M = 10 (k = source symbols of the heavy blob, n = coded symbols, u = usable slots per window, F = frame auth bytes; cell `k/n (u, F B)`; full table `raw/proto_alloc_cloud-vm-4core.csv`). Every mode gets the same M slots per message, the same slot capacity (`cap_regular`, and on C-V2X the certificate-bearing slot every 5th BSM, whose remaining capacity is cap - certificate and is usually below F, so it carries no authentication data): the allocation row is identical across modes except for the split of the same bytes.

SLH-DSA is only usable where the batch/anchor amortises the signature (merkle, chain rows above) or the budget is large (J3161).

### Hypothesis tests: chain vs erasure-coded per-message signatures (`frag_mds`)

Rule. Cell = (profile, PQ scheme, M, loss condition) with loss > 0 (i.i.d. [0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3] and Gilbert-Elliott conditions present). Seeds are paired (the same loss mask is applied to every mode). For each cell d = metric(chain) - metric(frag_mds) is computed per seed; the cell is a **win** for the chain if the mean difference is in the favourable direction, larger than 3 SE of d and larger than a minimum effect (share 0.005, bytes 1%, delay 1%, join 1%), a **loss** if the same holds in the other direction, otherwise a **tie**. Share: a mode that cannot run (infeasible) has share 0. Delay/join/bytes are compared only where both modes authenticate at least one message in every seed. **Verdict per hypothesis: supported if wins >= 2 x losses and wins > 0; refuted if losses >= 2 x wins and losses > 0; otherwise inconclusive.** This rule was fixed before looking at the data.

### Closed forms as a cross-check

Source: `raw/loss_crosscheck_cloud-vm-4core.csv`. `lib/pqsig/lossform.py` was updated to the symmetric model (erasure-coded anchor over the epoch's slots, anchor wait, the certificate-slot pattern, exact correlation of tag, key and anchor events) and is compared with the measured share under i.i.d. loss. z = (measured mean - closed form) / SE with SE = max(SE over seeds, binomial SE sqrt(c(1-c)/(seeds x N))); the binomial term only matters in near-deterministic cells where all seeds agree (disclosed rule, no hidden floor). Gilbert-Elliott loss has no closed form and is not compared.

1716 cells compared; **0 differ by more than 3 standard errors** (about 4.6 expected by chance); max |difference| = 0.0175. Modes with no closed form (symbol span > 255, continuity) are skipped: chain_lead_cont.

No cell disagrees: the implementation and the formula agree within sampling error wherever a formula exists.

## Q3: size or timing tail binding

Sources: `raw/oqs_timing_cloud-vm-4core.csv`, `raw/scoring_all_levels.csv`, `results/proto_summary.csv`. x86 VM only; MCU timings are not measured.

Method. Pairs = (lowest-level size class that was benchmarked, signature profile with a stated message rate; dns and the key-space profile excluded). Size-bound: the full signature exceeds the auth budget. Deadline = packet period (frame period if > 0, else message period). Timing-bound: max(p99 sign, p99 verify) of the class exceeds the deadline; classes with < 100 iterations have no usable tail, and are timing-bound only if the median alone exceeds the deadline, else `insufficient`. Family is size-bound if size-only pairs exceed timing-only pairs, timing-bound if the reverse, otherwise not distinguishing. Second look from the protocol runs: `tx_realtime_ratio > 1` (sender cannot keep up).

| family        |   size-only |   timing-only |   both |   neither |   insufficient |   pairs | family_binding     |
|:--------------|------------:|--------------:|-------:|----------:|---------------:|--------:|:-------------------|
| CROSS         |          30 |             0 |      0 |         0 |              0 |      30 | size               |
| Falcon/FN-DSA |           8 |             0 |      0 |         2 |              0 |      10 | size               |
| MAYO          |           5 |             0 |      0 |         5 |              0 |      10 | size               |
| ML-DSA        |           5 |             0 |      0 |         0 |              0 |       5 | size               |
| MQOM          |          20 |             0 |      0 |         0 |              0 |      20 | size               |
| SLH-DSA       |           7 |             0 |      3 |         0 |              0 |      10 | size               |
| SNOVA         |           3 |             0 |      0 |        12 |              0 |      15 | size               |
| UOV           |           0 |             0 |      0 |        20 |              0 |      20 | not distinguishing |

Figure `fig_q3_size_vs_tail.pdf` (source `raw/oqs_timing_cloud-vm-4core.csv`, `raw/scoring_all_levels.csv`).

Sender real-time check (protocol runs, M = 10): 0/202 feasible (profile, PQ, mode) configurations have a sender slower than the message rate.

**Verdict Q3: size is binding in 7 of 8 families, timing in 0, not distinguishing in 1** (rule above). Supported for x86 under this rule; inconclusive for constrained devices (no MCU data). Q3 is close to tautological because the deadlines are packet periods much longer than x86 operation times.

## Properties and limits (statements, not measurements)

- **The chain provides no non-repudiation.** Any receiver holding the disclosed key can compute valid tags, so a tag proves nothing to a third party. It therefore cannot replace signed messages where misbehaviour reporting or revocation needs attributable messages (e.g. V2X BSM signing); it is a bandwidth-saving channel authenticator, not a drop-in for signatures. Only the per-message signature and Merkle-batch modes give transferable evidence (Merkle: the signed root plus the path).
- **The chain needs loose time synchronisation** (the time-safety rule: a tag is accepted only if it arrived before its key could have been disclosed). The experiments assume zero clock error; a receiver with a manipulable clock is an attack surface (negative test T4 shows the check is what stops the late-key forgery).
- **Chain continuity across epochs: implemented** as `chain_lead_cont` (negative tests T5/T6). It makes an epoch's anchor loss survivable at the cost of 16 B per frame and exposes the chain to the usual 'one forged commitment poisons later epochs' risk only if a MAC could be forged (T6 shows a forged commitment is rejected).
- Hybrid: both signatures must verify (T7); stripping the classical half is rejected because the verifier requires both. Downgrade resistance beyond this is not analysed.
- Receivers keep the first-arrived symbol per index: a corrupted symbol can block a message (denial of service) but never causes acceptance.

## Runs still needed (on the user's own machines)

- `MACHINE_NAME=<name> ./run.sh` (full run) on every target machine; numbers here are `cloud-smoke` unless the tags above say otherwise. Publication numbers need a clean git tree (see `git_dirty`).
- Two-machine UDP run on a LAN: receiver `run_proto.py udp --role receiver --udp 0.0.0.0:9000 --keyfile K ...`, sender `--role sender --udp RECEIVER:9000 --start-delay 60 ...` with identical `--profile --pq --mode --M --seed`; copy the sender's keyfile to the receiver during the delay (see `udp_link.py`).
- MCU timings (Cortex-M) for the non-standardised families; measured loss traces of the real channels (the loss model here is i.i.d./Gilbert-Elliott); C-V2X PC5 Mode 4 scheduling, congestion and PDR (not modelled: slots are collision-free).
- TODO-RESULT inputs: certificate metadata size, per-message fragment-header sizes (the experiments charge their own explicit headers of 3-11 B + control fields, shown in the allocation table), BSM size for 437 B, LMS H=15/20 rows, remote_id/dns message rates.
- Items not implemented in this pass: reproduction of darzi2026a/junquera2023assessment/goertzen2022post overheads from their own testbeds; PQ-certificate chains with intermediate CAs; ZK-compressed signatures; pseudonym-certificate change.
